  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "This review critically evaluates pre-clinical animal models and their role in translation to clinical practice for cancer patients, discussing limitations and alternative strategies.",
  "what_it_found": "The average rate of successful translation from animal models to clinical cancer trials is less than 8%, with many failures attributed to differences in physiology and molecular targets between species.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "However, the average rate of successful translation from animal models to clinical cancer trials is less than 8%.",
      "topic": "Low translation rate"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Animal models are limited in their ability to mimic the extremely complex process of human carcinogenesis, physiology and progression.",
      "topic": "Model limitations"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Indeed, animal studies seem to overestimate by about 30% the likelihood that a treatment will be effective because negative results are often unpublished [9].",
      "topic": "Overestimation of efficacy"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Crucial genetic, molecular, immunologic and cellular differences between humans and mice prevent animal models from serving as effective means to seek for a cancer cure [13].",
      "topic": "Species differences"
    },
    {
      "quote": "The failure to translate from animals to humans is likely due in part to poor methodology and failure of the models to accurately mimic the human disease condition.",
      "topic": "Methodology and mimicry"
    },
    {
      "quote": "The vast majority of agents that are found to be successful in animal models do not pan out in human trials.",
      "topic": "General failure"
    }
  ]
